note: An internet survey listed 'fuzzy-matcher precision/recall' as a gap nothing hardened covers. Searching the tree first showed the house already had most of it: bench_decision_n1.py measures rank@1, recall, and a wrong-key count across a bar sweep; retrieval_quality.py the verbatim floor and compression recall; nestor.calibrate the false-serve half. The one thing unnamed was precision as a rate. bench/matcher_precision.py adds it by reusing the N1 scorer, and tests/test_matcher_precision.py gates it and the confusable failure IDEAS 6.106 named.

decisions.question: The matcher precision/recall 'gap' turned out to be mostly built already. Build a new harness, or add the missing piece to what exists?
decisions.commitment: Add the missing piece. bench/matcher_precision.py imports bench_decision_n1's corpus loader and scorer -- it re-scores nothing -- and derives the one metric the other benches leave implicit: precision as a rate (of the probes the matcher would serve at a bar, the fraction whose top candidate is the right decision), None when nothing is served. tests/test_matcher_precision.py gates precision 1.0 and recall >= 0.70 at the calibrated knee (bar 0.45), rank@1 >= 20/24, and asserts that below the knee (bar 0.30) the interrogative-stem confusables get served and precision drops under 1.0.
decisions.why: Precision is the number the serve gate actually turns on: the product's whole claim is that it does not serve a near-miss as verified, and precision at a bar is what that claim is worth. Rank@1 21/24 and precision 1.0 at bar 0.45 with recall 0.75 show the matcher ranks correctly and the shipped 0.92 bar -- which serves nothing on this corpus -- was the defect, not the matcher; that reproduces IDEAS 6.106 as a gate rather than a recalled figure. Reusing bench_decision_n1's scorer rather than writing a second one keeps this from becoming the vendored pair the repo refuses -- the same reason retrieval_quality delegates collisions to calibrate. Building a fresh harness would have rediscovered what four files already measured; the value was the one derived rate they did not name.
